the use of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin-receptor blockers (ARBs) is effective for reducing the incidence of proteinuria and cerebral edema, but that the use of ACE inhibitors or ARBs alone does not appear to be sufficient to prevent the recurrence of cerebral edema and renal damage once these have already appeared.
